# META — Catalysts

## TL;DR

Q1 2026 earnings (Apr 29 AH) remain the controlling catalyst on Day 4 of the post-print re-rating window. Capex guidance raised to **$125–145B** (nearly double FY2025's $72B) drove the stock −8.6% from $669 to ~$600 on 3.26x average volume. JPMorgan downgraded to Neutral ($725 PT). No new binary until Q2 2026 earnings (expected late July). **Macro context worsened on May 4:** Iran peace talks that briefly supported risk-on mood on May 1 reversed to reported missile strikes on a US warship near Jask island — oil prices higher, Dow futures lower, risk-off regime restored. (source: web_research/META.json, signals_combined.json, run 20260504_143030)

## Live catalysts

| Event | Date | Significance |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 2026 post-earnings re-rating window | Apr 29 – ~May 9 | HIGH — institutions still absorbing capex shock; multiple compression ongoing |
| Iran escalation (active military conflict) | May 4 ongoing | HIGH NEGATIVE — reversed May 1 peace-talks risk-on; oil >$100/bbl; Strait of Hormuz tail risk |
| Fed Chair transition (Powell → Warsh) | May 15 | MEDIUM NEGATIVE — hawkish succession candidate; policy uncertainty for high-multiple tech |
| Layoff restructuring (~8,000 employees / 10% workforce) | May 20 start | MEDIUM — signals cost pressure; offsets small amount of capex concern |
| Muse Spark AI model rollout | Ongoing from Apr 8 | MEDIUM positive — 4th on AI Index v4.0; losing ground to Alphabet's Cloud AI monetization |
| Social media addiction litigation | Ongoing | HIGH NEGATIVE — CA 70% liability verdict; 10,000+ suits; NM $375M award; no resolution timeline |
| Q2 2026 earnings | ~late July 2026 | MEDIUM — Q2 capex commentary and ad revenue acceleration are the key watch items |

## Recent news (as of May 4, 2026)

**Capex shock (HIGH):** Full-year capex raised to $125–145B at Q1 2026 earnings. No cloud revenue stream (unlike Alphabet, MSFT, Amazon) makes the spend harder to justify near-term. Free cash flow compression expected 2–3 years. Analysts debating whether this is Metaverse 2.0 repeat or a real AI moat-build. (source: web_research/META.json, run 20260504_143030)

**JPMorgan downgrade (HIGH NEGATIVE):** Downgraded April 30 to Neutral, PT $725, citing capex outweighing solid Q1 results and intensifying full-stack AI competition. Street consensus remains broadly bullish (36–40 analysts, avg PT ~$836.81) but was formed pre-capex absorption — further downgrades possible. (source: web_research/META.json, run 20260504_143030)

**Iran escalation (HIGH — macro negative for META):** May 4 missile strikes on US warship reversed May 1 peace-talks optimism. Crude oil above $100/bbl; Strait of Hormuz closure risk active. This is directly negative for high-multiple growth tech. (source: web_research/META.json macro_context, run 20260504_143030)

**Muse Spark (MEDIUM positive):** Proprietary LLM from Meta Superintelligence Labs led by Alexandr Wang. Competitor contrast: Alphabet reported Google Cloud +63% YoY to $20B — META's AI narrative continues to lag on monetization proof. (source: web_research/META.json, run 20260504_143030)

**Layoffs (MEDIUM):** ~8,000 employees (10% of workforce) starting May 20; 6,000 open roles frozen. Cost discipline signal, but reinforces that capex pressure is real — offsetting AI staff with layoffs is cost-neutral at best. (source: web_research/META.json, run 20260504_143030)

## Lessons

2026-04-30 | NVDA | EMA pullback Fib dip-buy | -$63.20 (corrected from -$264.65) | Stop triggered at $205.30 (hourly Fib 61.8%); swing_trend_momentum and swing_breakout were bullish on AI capex thesis, but price breached the stop zone intraday amid stretched macro (RSI 81–87) with no bullish confirmation candle before exit. **Note:** trade was originally sized 67 shares ($14,020) due to a phantom $100K budget bug (fixed commit b2b472d).
